assignment_rule: A neuron's family is the family holding the majority of its connections; a neuron with no majority family (fresh, or scrambled by a per-connection crossover) draws one weighted by its own connections per eligible family, i.e. for a fresh uniform neuron P(family) = the family's share of the encoded bits ('my first connection picks the family'). Aggregate wiring per family therefore matches spread; only its concentration changes.
fallback: A family is a HOME for a w-bit neuron only if it has at least w - floor(rf_cross*w) distinct ENCODED bits (after ids_encoding_dedupe, if on). A smaller family is reachable at that width only through the cross budget; a neuron whose width no family can host is exempt (left as drawn). Nothing is ever placed out-of-family to cover a deficit, so a projected neuron's family always holds a strict majority of its connections (rf_cross < 0.5).
notes: Upper/lower-case spellings are both listed: the HF random split uses Sload/Dload/Djit/res_bdy_len, the temporal split sload/dload/djit/response_body_len.
proto/service/state are categorical (log2(#categories) bits), so protocol is a small family on the legacy list (~12 encoded bits): at wide neurons it is reachable only via the cross budget.

ttl_state merge_into context (Luiz, IDS-55 follow-up): with ids_encoding_dedupe on, ttl_state keeps ~15 encoded bits (sttl/dttl/ct_state_ttl have few distinct values), too few to host a neuron, so it joins context (UNSW's connection-window counters; ct_state_ttl is itself a window feature). Dedupe off: 196 bits on unswr, no merge, map unchanged.

v2 (Luiz 08/11, after the IDS-55 unswt A/B ran on v1): handshake merge_into timing (tcprtt/synack/ackdat ARE the setup round-trip timings; ~10 bits with dedupe on) and protocol merge_into context (~12 bits even with dedupe off on the legacy list). protocol merges on dedupe-OFF maps too, so this is a new version (test cache re-keys); v1 stays as the A/B's provenance.

ttl_state.why: Hop count / OS fingerprint of each side plus the connection state machine; ct_state_ttl is UNSW's own joint feature of the two, so the four move together.

handshake.why: TCP setup timing (SYN-SYNACK-ACK) and the header fields fixed at setup (window advertisement, initial sequence numbers). Every non-TCP flow reads 0 in all of them, so they co-vary by construction.

volume.why: How much each side sent: bytes, packets, mean packet size, retransmitted/dropped packets, HTTP response body size.

rate.why: Throughput: bits per second per direction and the overall packet rate.

timing.why: Time structure of the flow: duration, inter-packet arrival, jitter.

context.why: UNSW's 100-connection window counters (same service/host/port pairs) and the same-address flag: what the surrounding traffic looks like, not this flow.

protocol.why: Which protocol / application the flow speaks and what it does in it (HTTP methods, FTP commands and login, pipelined transaction depth).
